description: Replace both install destinations by atomic rename from a staged temp in the destination directory, so reinstalling over a running gship stops poisoning the image (macOS SIGKILL) and stops exposing a torn read

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms bun test's per-test timeout default is 5000 ms and that the only global override is the --timeout CLI flag, so a long fixture-compiling leg must declare its own timeout in source (this repo runs plain `bun test`, no bunfig.toml). Also confirms the per-test options-object form (`test(name, { ... }, fn)`) is supported alongside the trailing-number form, and that under CLAUDECODE=1 bun hides per-test pass lines but KEEPS the summary counters, which is why the acceptance oracles grep the 'N pass' / '0 fail' summary lines rather than per-test output.

userStories.title: Swap install.sh destinations by atomic rename from a staged temp inside INSTALL_DIR
userStories.description: As someone reinstalling gateship while a `gship run` session is live, I need install.sh to replace ${DEST} by renaming a fully prepared staged file over it instead of writing into the destination in place, so the running process keeps its old inode (no SIGKILL at the next exec, no ETXTBSY abort on linux) and no reader can ever observe a partially written binary.
acceptanceCriteria: install.sh stages one temp file per NAME with mktemp INSIDE ${INSTALL_DIR} (never $TMPDIR, whose rename would cross filesystems on the linux targets where /tmp is usually tmpfs), using a 6-X template both BSD and GNU mktemp accept. [oracle: file-assert grep -qE 'mktemp[[:space:]]+"\$\{INSTALL_DIR\}/\.' install.sh]

No cp writes directly to ${DEST} and no rm targets ${DEST}: an 'rm -f then cp' fix clears the SIGKILL but keeps the torn-read window that is the issue's second symptom, so it must not be the shape that lands. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*cp[[:space:]].*"\$\{DEST\}"[[:space:]]*$' install.sh && ! grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*rm[[:space:]].*"\$\{DEST\}"' install.sh]

The only write to ${DEST} is an mv -f from the staged file (mv -f and not bare mv, because BSD mv prompts when the destination is unwritable and stdin is a tty, which hangs a terminal-run ./install.sh), and chmod +x plus the darwin quarantine strip both act on the staged file, so the destination is never observable non-executable or quarantined. [oracle: file-assert grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*mv -f[[:space:]].*"\$\{DEST\}"[[:space:]]*$' install.sh && ! grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*(chmod|xattr)[[:space:]].*"\$\{DEST\}"' install.sh]

The existing EXIT trap is EXTENDED to also remove the staged file rather than joined by a second trap on EXIT (a second one replaces the first and leaks TMP_BIN/TMP_SUMS), and it uses the bash-3.2-safe ${STAGED:+...} scalar form instead of an array expansion, which errors on an empty array under set -u in macOS bash 3.2.57. [oracle: file-assert grep -qE "^trap 'rm -f .*TMP_BIN.*TMP_SUMS.*STAGED" install.sh && grep -qF 'STAGED:+' install.sh]

A durable leg in test/install-sh.test.ts whose name contains 'running binary' runs the REAL install.sh over an ${INSTALL_DIR}/gship that a live process is currently executing, and asserts the CONJUNCTION of three things: install exits 0, the live process survives, and the file left at ${INSTALL_DIR}/gship still executes successfully. Never a darwin-only SIGKILL-code assertion: main is RED on both platforms for different reasons (darwin poisons the mapped image while install still exits 0; linux refuses the cp with ETXTBSY and set -e aborts mid-loop, leaving gateship installed and gship not). [oracle: OUT="$(bun test test/install-sh.test.ts -t 'running binary' 2>&1)"; echo "$OUT" | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$OUT" | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*0 fail']

A second durable leg whose name contains 'atomic swap' installs twice into the same INSTALL_DIR and asserts the directory entry was replaced rather than the inode rewritten (the inode differs between run 1 and run 2; plain cp was measured preserving the destination inode), that the installed binary is still executable (mktemp creates 0600, so a fix that forgets to chmod the staged file regresses here), and that INSTALL_DIR is left with no leftover dot-file staging litter. [oracle: OUT="$(bun test test/install-sh.test.ts -t 'atomic swap' 2>&1)"; echo "$OUT" | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$OUT" | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*0 fail']

The new legs are falsifiable rather than tautological: pointed at main's install.sh they go RED. The test resolves the script path through a GATESHIP_TEST_INSTALL_SH env override that defaults to the repo copy, so the reviewer can re-run the sweep independently. [oracle: bash -c 'git show main:install.sh > "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cam497-main-install.sh" && ! GATESHIP_TEST_INSTALL_SH="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cam497-main-install.sh" bun test test/install-sh.test.ts -t "running binary"']

Neither new leg carries a skip guard (test.skip / it.skip / .skipIf / .todo): the host lane requires zero skips (test/helpers/lane-expectations.json) and the CAM-424 precedent (test/integration/self-invoke-compiled.test.ts) says an unavailable `bun build --compile` is not a tolerated skip condition. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -qE '(test|it|describe)\.(skip|skipIf|todo)' test/install-sh.test.ts]

Each new leg declares an explicit timeout, because bun's per-test default is 5000 ms and this repo has no bunfig.toml, while compiling a fixture with bun build --compile plus two real install runs exceeds it; the house forms are a trailing 15_000 argument or a { timeout: 30_000 } options object. [oracle: file-assert grep -qE 'timeout:[[:space:]]*[0-9_]+|,[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9_]{3,}[[:space:]]*\)' test/install-sh.test.ts]

install.sh's header block documents that the destination is swapped by atomic rename from a staged temp and WHY (a running image is poisoned on macOS and killed at the next exec; linux refuses the in-place write with ETXTBSY), consistent with ADR-0058. Presence-grep proves only that the text is not empty; prose fidelity is the reviewer's call. [oracle: file-assert grep -qiE 'atomic rename|rename\(2\)' install.sh && grep -qF 'ETXTBSY' install.sh]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
The lint and static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes:
Files: install.sh (trap at :83 and :98, install loop at :136-148), test/install-sh.test.ts (8 existing legs, all offline via a curl PATH-shim; reuse that machinery).

REFERENCE SHAPE, already hand-applied and swept green by the operator on 2026-08-04: declare STAGED="" BEFORE the loop; EXTEND the :98 trap to `trap 'rm -f "${TMP_BIN}" "${TMP_SUMS}" ${STAGED:+"${STAGED}"}' EXIT`; inside the loop STAGED="$(mktemp "${INSTALL_DIR}/.${NAME}.XXXXXX")", cp TMP_BIN -> STAGED, chmod +x STAGED, xattr on STAGED, mv -f STAGED DEST, then STAGED="". A scalar and not an array is load-bearing (macOS /bin/bash is 3.2.57; "${ARR[@]}" on an empty array errors under set -u, while ${STAGED:+"${STAGED}"} is 3.2-safe). mktemp needs the directory to exist, which holds only because `mkdir -p "${INSTALL_DIR}"` already precedes the loop. Permissions do not change: TMP_BIN is mktemp 0600 plus chmod +x = 0700 today and the staged file ends the same.

THE FIX WRITTEN IN THE ISSUE BODY DOES NOT WORK AS WRITTEN: TMP_BIN is a bare mktemp in $TMPDIR (:82), not in INSTALL_DIR, and the cp sits in a loop writing TWO destinations per run, so `mv ${TMP_BIN} ${DEST}` consumes the source on the first iteration and breaks the second, and is not atomic when $TMPDIR is a different filesystem. Stage per NAME inside INSTALL_DIR.

FIXTURE RULES (each one measured; violating any turns the sweep into a false result): use `bun build --compile` for the live target, because a copy of /bin/sleep or any Apple platform binary dies by AMFI on arm64 even after a clean rename to a new inode, which would read as 'the fix does not work'. Re-sign the compiled fixture with `codesign --force --sign -` on darwin (scripts/build-release.sh:100-106 documents the raw-artifact invalid-signature confound) before using it. Compile inside a scratch cwd, `( cd "$SCRATCH" && bun build --compile ... )`, because bun spills .bun-build into the CWD and not the outfile dir (the 9.97 GB accumulation in the repo root is CAM-407, out of scope here). Reuse the SAME compiled binary for both roles (pre-existing running target and served asset): identical bytes still poison, measured shasum-identical with one path rc=137 and the other rc=0, so no second payload is needed.

HANDSHAKE, NOT SLEEP: the fixture must write a ready-marker file from inside itself after exec, and the test must wait for that marker before running install.sh. If install runs before the image is mapped, main PASSES and the leg is a false GREEN. Poll with the repo's waitForCondition idiom, never a fixed setTimeout (scripts/check-test-sleeps.ts gates this). Every spawned child needs stdin redirected from /dev/null.

CURL SHIM (patterns.md:1198, :1205, :1211): parse args by `prev == "-o"` and never by position, because install.sh puts the URL BEFORE -o; the fake manifest line needs TWO literal spaces since install.sh greps -F "  ${ASSET}"; compute the digest live from the bytes just served using install.sh's own probe order (sha256sum then shasum -a 256), never a frozen literal (patterns.md:1209); GATESHIP_VERSION short-circuits tag resolution at install.sh:61 and removes the releases-list call. runInstallSh replaces the child env wholesale (no HOME), which is why GATESHIP_INSTALL_DIR is mandatory under set -u.

Add the GATESHIP_TEST_INSTALL_SH seam as a one-line default on INSTALL_SCRIPT; it is test-only and exists so the red-against-main sweep is reproducible by the reviewer instead of being a one-shot claim in the worker report.

Do NOT add a --version smoke to install.sh: that is CAM-496's class (artifact incompatible with the host) and has its own issue. Domain vocabulary for this change is already on main: CONTEXT.md 'staged install temp' and 'atomic install swap', plus ADR-0058.

userStories.title: Stage, verify, then atomically rename in build-release.sh --install, and make the docs match
userStories.description: As a developer installing a locally built gateship with ./scripts/build-release.sh --install, I need the artifact fully prepared and verified (quarantine cleared, re-signed, signature verified, --version smoked) BEFORE it is renamed over the destination, so a failed verification leaves my previous installation intact instead of destroyed and a live gship keeps running.
acceptanceCriteria: In the --install branch of scripts/build-release.sh no cp writes directly to ${DEST}; the artifact is staged with mktemp inside ${DEST_DIR} and the destination is replaced with mv -f. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*cp[[:space:]].*"\$\{DEST\}"[[:space:]]*$' scripts/build-release.sh && grep -qE 'mktemp[[:space:]]+"\$\{DEST_DIR\}/\.' scripts/build-release.sh && grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*mv -f[[:space:]].*"\$\{DEST\}"[[:space:]]*$' scripts/build-release.sh]

Every preparation and verification step names the STAGED file and never the destination: xattr -cr, codesign --force --sign -, codesign -v, chmod, and the --version smoke. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*(xattr|codesign|chmod)[[:space:]].*"\$\{DEST\}"' scripts/build-release.sh && ! grep -qF '"${DEST}" --version' scripts/build-release.sh]

test/build-release-smoke.test.ts pins the ordering in a describe block whose name contains 'atomic rename': each step's position is derived from the --install loop text at read time (indexOf over the script source), never a frozen line number, and every step is asserted to precede the mv. The deliberate consequence is asserted rather than left implicit: a failed verification now leaves the previous installation intact. [oracle: OUT="$(bun test test/build-release-smoke.test.ts -t 'atomic rename' 2>&1)"; echo "$OUT" | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$OUT" | grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*0 fail']
No assertion in the ordering block compares a derived index against a frozen literal position. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -qE 'toBeLessThan\([0-9]' test/build-release-smoke.test.ts]

The ordering block is falsifiable rather than tautological: pointed at main's scripts/build-release.sh it goes RED. The test resolves the script path through a GATESHIP_TEST_BUILD_RELEASE_SH env override defaulting to the repo copy, so the reviewer can re-run the sweep independently. [oracle: bash -c 'git show main:scripts/build-release.sh > "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cam497-main-br.sh" && ! GATESHIP_TEST_BUILD_RELEASE_SH="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cam497-main-br.sh" bun test test/build-release-smoke.test.ts -t "atomic rename"']

The single existing EXIT trap is EXTENDED to also clear a leftover staged file, never joined by a second trap on EXIT (which would replace the first and leak SMOKE_DIR), so an aborted verification leaves no .gateship.XXXXXX behind in the destination directory. [oracle: file-assert grep -qE "^trap 'rm -rf .*SMOKE_DIR.*STAGED.*' EXIT" scripts/build-release.sh]

scripts/build-release.sh's header documents the atomic-rename install and that verification runs before the swap. Presence-grep proves only that the text is not empty; prose fidelity is the reviewer's call. [oracle: file-assert grep -qiE 'atomic rename|rename\(2\)' scripts/build-release.sh]

README's install descriptions are coherent with the rename semantics: neither the packaged-binary option nor the build-from-source option still describes the install as copying over the destination. The `sudo cp` examples for /usr/local/bin are deliberately untouched (human-run examples, out of scope). [oracle: file-assert ! grep -qE 'copies to ~/\.local/bin|copies to \$\{?HOME\}?/\.local/bin' README.md && grep -qiE 'atomic rename|renamed into place|rename\(2\)' README.md]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]

The lint and static spine passes (bun run check:all), including the file-size ratchet: if test/build-release-smoke.test.ts grows past its ceiling, scripts/file-size-budget.json is raised in the same change with a CAM-497 tracker reference and the _ref field restated, which scripts/check-file-sizes.ts requires of any raise diff. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes:
Files: scripts/build-release.sh (--install branch at :192-218, existing EXIT trap at :176), test/build-release-smoke.test.ts (121-line budget ceiling, currently 120 lines), README.md (packaged-binary section around :30-60 and the build-from-source block around :130-145), scripts/file-size-budget.json.

SHAPE: STAGED="$(mktemp "${DEST_DIR}/.${NAME}.XXXXXX")"; cp HOST_BIN -> STAGED; xattr -cr STAGED; codesign --force --sign - STAGED; codesign -v STAGED; chmod +x STAGED; SMOKE_ACTUAL="$("${STAGED}" --version)" compared to EXPECTED; only then mv -f STAGED DEST and clear STAGED. Same bash-3.2 scalar rule as US-001: ${STAGED:+"${STAGED}"}, never an array.

WHY THIS SITE LOOKED HEALTHY: it has the same direct cp over the destination as install.sh, but the `codesign --force` immediately after rewrites the file and repairs the poisoned image, so the internal path MASKS the defect instead of not having it. Once the codesign moves to the staged file (where it belongs), the masking is gone and the rename is what makes it correct.

GOTCHA THAT WILL BREAK AN EXISTING TEST: test/build-release-smoke.test.ts asserts the trap's exact text with /trap\s+'rm -rf "\$\{SMOKE_DIR:-\}"'\s+EXIT/. Extending the trap body breaks that regex, so update that existing assertion in the same change rather than adding a second trap to keep it green: a second trap on EXIT replaces the first and would silently stop cleaning SMOKE_DIR.

The file already has a static-source-guard precedent to mirror for the new block (the CAM-495 SHA256SUMS describe at :87-120 derives indexes with indexOf and compares them to each other, never to a literal). Add GATESHIP_TEST_BUILD_RELEASE_SH the same way US-001 adds GATESHIP_TEST_INSTALL_SH, defaulting to the resolved repo path, so the red-against-main sweep is reproducible.

Out of scope and must not creep in: the README `sudo cp dist/... /usr/local/bin` examples, CAM-485 (auto-update), CAM-496 (install-time --version smoke), CAM-407 (.bun-build accumulation).

patterns.md:1207 is relevant to the ordering block: an ordering oracle that greps for one marker appearing textually before another is satisfied by source-line position and not by runtime control flow, so put the new code physically where the assertion expects it instead of relying on where it logically belongs.
